sentences.en: It's not really, uh, or evidence-based practice or psychotherapy, the thing that I do for a living, any of that still don't get that one.

sentences.zh: 他们会想，好吧，如果它做了这件事，那这件事要对意识负责吗？

sentences.zh: 然后其他神经科学家的反应是：可能不会。

sentences.en: There might be another thing that we can't see yet.
sentences.zh: 可能还有另一个我们目前还看不到的东西。

sentences.en: And they're like, well, you demand evidence for everything.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会说，好吧，你们对什么都要索取证据。

sentences.zh: 所以如果你没有别的解释，也许这就是我的解释。

sentences.zh: 我觉得你大概是错的。

sentences.en: You know, the big debate, you can look at the blog, but this is a thing.

sentences.en: There's a lot of neuroscientists that have kind of run with that.

sentences.zh: 我认为这些理论很有趣，我们也应该顺着他们的思路想想。

sentences.en: I don't really buy any of them in one direction, but, you know, medicine ran on results, replication and reasonable safety protocols for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我个人并不完全倾向于其中任何一方，但是，你知道的，医学长期以来靠的是结果、可复制性以及合理的安全规程来运转。

sentences.en: And psychology is this one field that demands that we have to understand why something works before we will admit that it works.
sentences.zh: 而心理学却是这样一个领域：它要求我们必须先理解某个东西为什么管用，然后才肯承认它管用。

sentences.en: Having made that statement though, I don't think that's true.
sentences.zh: 不过话说回来，我认为事实并非如此。

sentences.en: What I see is a very insecure field that only does that when I don't want you to be right.
sentences.zh: 我看到的是一个极度缺乏安全感的领域，它只在“我不想让你是对的”时候才会这么做。

sentences.en: This is only a position that is used from people who are in power to say, I don't want the mechanism of action that I use or that I think that

sentences.zh: 自己正在使用的作用机制。

sentences.en: Or I don't want the field to change.
sentences.zh: 或者我不想让这个领域发生改变。

sentences.zh: 我不想让研究发生改变。

sentences.en: And so I'm going to demand that you know why the effective thing that you are doing is correct.
sentences.zh: 因此，我要要求你证明你所做的那个有效的事情为什么是正确的。

sentences.en: I don't know, man, I'm just doing it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，老兄，我只是在照做而已。

sentences.en: And I'm not talking to those people.
sentences.zh: 我不是在对那些人说话。

sentences.en: I'm just saying this is a pattern that happens in the 60s, 70s, 80s, 90s, and the odds in psychotherapy.
sentences.zh: 我只是在指出一种在20世纪60、70、80、90年代以及2000年代的心理治疗中一再发生的模式。

sentences.en: And it gets worse every time where we pretend that, oh, we're totally open to no ideas.
sentences.zh: 而且每一次情况都变得更糟，我们假装，哦，我们对新观点完全持开放态度。

sentences.en: We love science.
sentences.zh: 我们热爱科学。

sentences.en: We love evidence-based practice.
sentences.zh: 我们热爱循证实践。

sentences.en: You just have to understand exactly what the brain is doing before we can do it in the room where I talk to a person.
sentences.zh: 你只需要在我和一个人对话的那个房间里进行实践之前，先确切地弄明白大脑到底在做什么。

sentences.en: Well, it's never worked that way before.
sentences.zh: 好吧，以前从来没有这样运作过。

sentences.en: And it will not really probably ever work that way anytime soon.
sentences.zh: 而且在不久的将来，大概也永远不会以这种方式运作。

sentences.en: So maybe we should just keep doing it the way that we did it before, like 1980, when all of the mental health outcomes started to get worse every year forever and ever,
sentences.zh: 所以也许我们应该像以前那样继续做，就像1980年那样，当时所有的心理健康结果开始年复一年地变得越来越糟，

sentences.en: even though medicine got more and more and more evidence-based.
sentences.zh: 尽管医学变得越来越具有循证依据。

sentences.en: And before you email me and say, you can't control for a study where like, you know, that everyone in 1980 is doing the same thing that they are in like 2026.

sentences.en: And so we don't know that psychotherapy getting worse is the thing that made psychotherapy outcomes get worse.
sentences.zh: “因此我们并不知道心理治疗效果变差究竟是不是心理治疗本身变差导致的。”——

sentences.en: Neither can you.
sentences.zh: 你同样也做不到。

sentences.en: The bodies that fell, the roots that were dug from the earth so these games could be played.

sentences.en: In 1936, a psychologist named Saul Rosenzweig noticed something embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 1936年，一位名叫索尔·罗森茨威格的心理学家注意到了一件令人尴尬的事。

sentences.en: Every school of therapy had a different theory of mind.
sentences.zh: 每一个治疗学派都有着不同的心灵理论。

sentences.en: The theories that contradicted each other and all the therapies worked about equally well, even though they contradicted.
sentences.zh: 这些理论彼此矛盾，然而所有的治疗方法效果都差不多，尽管它们彼此矛盾。

sentences.en: The Adlerians were looking at things like birth order and relational energy and, um, you know, compensation.
sentences.zh: 阿德勒学派关注的是诸如出生顺序、关系能量以及，嗯，你知道的，代偿之类的事情。

sentences.en: The Freudians were looking at how sex was being projected or the need for sex or the need for power.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德学派探讨的是性欲是如何被投射出来的，或者是对性欲的需求，又或是对权力的需求。

sentences.en: And the Jungians were looking at like a holistic life cycle process, uh, sort of fused with evolutionary psychology.
sentences.zh: 而荣格学派则着眼于某种整体生命周期的过程，嗯，有点像是与进化心理学融合在一起。

sentences.en: He borrowed a line from Alice in Wonderland where the Dodo judges a race by announcing that everyone has won and all must have prizes.
sentences.zh: 他借用了《爱丽丝梦游仙境》中的一个桥段，其中渡渡鸟通过宣布“每个人都赢了，而且所有人都必须有奖品”来判定一场赛跑的胜负。

sentences.en: The Dodo verdict has held for 90 years.
sentences.zh: 渡渡鸟的这个裁决已经维持了90年。

sentences.en: In the modern meta-analysis, the specific type of therapy explains somewhere between zero and one percent of how well therapy goes.
sentences.zh: 在现代的元分析中，特定类型的疗法只能解释心理治疗效果的百分之零到百分之一。

sentences.en: The Freudians, Jungians, Adlerians, and now all the modern types of therapy all have, um,
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德学派、荣格学派、阿德勒学派，以及现在所有的现代疗法，都有着，嗯，

sentences.en: conflicting assumptions, not just about what the therapy is effective or like how it should be done,
sentences.zh: 相互冲突的假设，不仅关于这种疗法是否有效或应该如何进行，

sentences.en: but about the very way that the mind works and what the point or the purpose or mechanisms of healing are.
sentences.zh: 还关于心灵运作的根本方式，以及治愈的意义、目的或机制是什么。

sentences.en: And yet when you do them, these different therapies all seem to work equally well across different types of therapists for different types of issues.
sentences.zh: 然而，当你应用这些不同的疗法时，对于不同类型的治疗师和不同类型的问题，它们似乎都同样有效。

sentences.en: And the field treats that as a scandal.
sentences.zh: 而整个心理学界却把这当作一桩丑闻。

sentences.en: It was the answer that was, you know, always sort of underneath everything that they were researching.
sentences.zh: 这个答案其实，你知道的，一直隐藏在他们所研究的一切事物的底层。

sentences.en: Um, but it wasn't the thing that they were supposed to research or it wasn't the way that research was supposed to work.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但这不是他们本该去研究的东西，或者说这并不是研究本来应该发挥的作用。

sentences.en: You know, the id is not a real thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，本我并不是一个真实存在的东西。

sentences.en: Neither is the schema, you know, the inner part or the archetype.
sentences.zh: 图式也不是，你知道的，那种内在部分或是原型。

sentences.en: If you open a skull, you're not going to find an inner critic.
sentences.zh: 如果你切开头骨，你是找不到一个内在的批判者的。

sentences.en: You're not going to find a wounded child.
sentences.zh: 你也找不到一个受伤的小孩。

sentences.zh: 你找不到治疗师们长期以来一直使用的任何隐喻。

sentences.en: They're different alphabets for writing down the same activity.
sentences.zh: 它们只是用来记录同一种活动的不同字母表。

sentences.en: They are different metaphors, metaphorical lenses for looking at dynamic processes that are so vastly complicated.
sentences.zh: 它们是不同的隐喻，是观察那些极其复杂的动态过程的隐喻性透镜。

sentences.en: We can't understand them without a reductive containing metaphor.
sentences.zh: 如果没有一个具有概括性的简约隐喻，我们根本无法理解它们。

sentences.zh: 当你谈论美洲原住民时，他们相信某种类似于玉米神灵的东西，当

sentences.en: In the 90s, insurance companies started requiring randomized trials before they would pay for a therapy.
sentences.zh: 在90年代，保险公司开始要求在为某种疗法付费之前必须进行随机对照试验。

sentences.en: You know, the standard trial needs a manual, a fixed number of weeks, a single diagnosis, and an outcome that you can put a form on.

sentences.en: And only one family of therapies was built around those manuals.

sentences.en: Not because the evidence was better, but because the trials were able to be done.

sentences.en: And when researchers finally ask patients what they got out of therapy.

sentences.zh: 在177项研究中，患者几乎很少提及症状评分。

sentences.en: They talked about understanding themselves and feeling in charge of their own lives.
sentences.zh: 他们谈论的是理解了自我，并感受到了对自己生活的掌控。

sentences.en: The measuring system had been pointed for 50 years at the one outcome that patients were treating as a side effect.
sentences.zh: 这套评估系统在过去的50年里，一直对准了患者们仅仅当作副作用的那个单一结果。

sentences.en: And some of the strongest evidence for all of this is printed in the methods sections of the studies.
sentences.zh: 而所有这一切最有力的一些证据，其实就印在这些研究的方法部分中。

sentences.en: Before many antidepressant trials start, everyone who signs up gets a sugar pill for a week or two.
sentences.zh: 在许多抗抑郁药试验开始之前，每个报名的人都会连续一两周吃糖丸。

sentences.en: Without being told.
sentences.zh: 在不知情的情况下。

sentences.en: And the people who get better are removed from the study.
sentences.zh: 而那些好转的人则会被移出研究。

sentences.en: And it's called a placebo run-in.
sentences.zh: 这被称为安慰剂导入期。

sentences.en: And it is standard because when you give suffering people a doctor, a schedule, a bottle of
sentences.zh: 这是标准做法，因为当你给遭受痛苦的人提供一位医生、一个时间表、一瓶

sentences.en: pills, and someone who writes their pain down and listens to them, a huge number of them will just start healing.
sentences.zh: 药，以及一个会把他们的痛苦记录下来并倾听他们说话的人时，其中绝很大一部分人就会开始康复。

sentences.en: people who did not improve on the placebo.
sentences.zh: 那些服用安慰剂后没有改善的人。

sentences.en: And then they run the trial again, a study population
sentences.zh: 然后他们再次进行试验，这是一组

sentences.en: selected at, you know, a lot of expense.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，花费巨大才筛选出来的研究人群。

sentences.en: These are expensive things for being unable to benefit
sentences.zh: 这些都是高成本的事情，仅仅是为了无法从

sentences.en: from being cared for.
sentences.zh: 关怀中受益而付出代价。

sentences.en: We throw out all of these patients who heal.
sentences.zh: 我们抛弃了所有这些康复了的患者。

sentences.en: And what survives, that filtering is very small.
sentences.zh: 经过这种筛选，留存下来的样本非常小。

sentences.en: Across more than 200 trials in 70,000 patients, the drug moved the standard depression scale about 10 points and the sugar pill about eight.
sentences.zh: 在7万名患者参与的200多项试验中，药物将标准抑郁量表降低了大约10分，而糖丸则降低了大约8分。

sentences.en: The smallest change a patient can feel is about three.
sentences.zh: 患者能感受到的最小变化大约是3分。

sentences.en: The drugs win reliably, you know, a race that nobody can feel them winning.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，药物稳操胜券，赢得了一场没有人能感受到它们在赢的比赛。

sentences.en: And sugar pills have no side effects.
sentences.zh: 而且糖丸没有任何副作用。

sentences.en: So patients on the real drug can tell you which group they're in, which is the exact same crime that the FDA convicted MDMA of in that part one series that we were talking about.
sentences.zh: 因此服用真药的患者能分辨出自己属于哪一组，这跟我们在那期上集里谈到的、FDA给MDMA定罪的罪名完全一样。

sentences.en: When you gave someone MDMA, they could figure out that they were on a medication because the MDMA makes you trip.
sentences.zh: 当你给人服用MDMA时，他们能发现自己正在服用药物，因为MDMA会让你产生幻觉。

sentences.en: And so the FDA said, well, we can't really prove scientifically that this makes you get better,
sentences.zh: 因此FDA说，好吧，我们无法真正在科学上证明这能让你病情好转，

sentences.en: even though you're saying you are, because you could figure out that it wasn't sugar.
sentences.zh: 尽管你说你好了，因为你能分辨出那不是糖丸。

sentences.en: But I want to point out that antidepressants were always doing this too.
sentences.zh: 但我想要指出的是，抗抑郁药其实一直以来也都在这么做。

sentences.en: It's just that their side effects were a little quieter about it.
sentences.zh: 只不过它们的副作用在表现这一点上要稍微安静一些罢了。

sentences.en: You know, Ted Kapchick measured the thing that we keep throwing away.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，特德·卡普奇克（Ted Kaptchick）对我们一直抛弃的东西进行了测量。

sentences.en: He split patients with irritable bowel syndrome three ways, a wait list, fake acupuncture from a brisk practitioner who said almost nothing.
sentences.zh: 他将患有肠易激综合征的患者分成三组：候诊名单组，由一位动作麻利、几乎不说话的医生提供假针灸治疗组。

sentences.en: And then the same fake acupuncture, by fake, he means not real acupuncture, wasn't doing anything in the school of acupuncture with meridians.
sentences.zh: 然后是同样的假针灸——这里的“假”是指并非真正的针灸，不符合经络针灸学派的任何原理，

sentences.en: It was just somebody sort of putting random needles.
sentences.zh: 只是某人随便扎几根针而已。

sentences.en: But the same fake, in quotes, acupuncture from a warm practitioner who listened.
sentences.zh: 但同样是加了引号的“假”针灸，是由一位会倾听的温和医生来进行的。

sentences.en: And he said that he expected the patients would improve.
sentences.zh: 并且他说他预期患者会有所改善。

sentences.en: People who got the brisk and cold acupuncturist said that they felt slightly better.
sentences.zh: 接受动作麻利且冷漠的针灸师治疗的人表示他们感觉稍微好了一点。

sentences.en: But the person, the people who got acupuncture from a warm person who listened to them were some of the highest responders for many outcomes.
sentences.zh: 但是，那些从认真倾听他们的温和医生那里接受针灸治疗的人，在许多结果上成为了反应最好的人群之一。

sentences.en: I mean, those results were competing with what antidepressants do.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些结果足以与抗抑郁药的效果相媲美。

sentences.en: So in my field, it is this confound that the newest trials use remote raters who've never met the patient.
sentences.zh: 所以在我的领域里，存在这样一个混淆变量：最新的试验使用从未见过患者的远程评分员。

sentences.en: And so nobody can link warmth into the measurement or human interaction, all the things that psychotherapy is built on that those trials are supposed to be measuring.
sentences.zh: 因此，没有人能将温暖或人际互动融入到测量中，而这正是心理治疗所建立的基础，也是那些试验本该去测量的内容。

sentences.en: And his placebo research shows a couple of things that I'll extract.
sentences.zh: 他的安慰剂研究展示了几个我想提炼出来的要点。

sentences.en: Like first, you don't have to trick anybody.
sentences.zh: 比如首先，你不需要欺骗任何人。

sentences.en: You know, I make fun of myself and my models for being kind of cranky and the thing that I'm doing in therapy being kind of silly
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我经常取笑我自己和我的治疗模型有点古怪，我在治疗中做的事情也有点荒谬，

sentences.en: and then kind of explain the history of it and how we got here.
sentences.zh: 然后我会顺便解释一下它的历史以及我们是如何走到这一步的。

sentences.en: And like that is part of the cognitive intervention that I use that makes somebody feel comfortable and in control.
sentences.zh: 类似于这正是我所使用的认知干预的一部分，它能让人感到舒适和尽在掌控。

sentences.en: And like,
sentences.zh: 而且，

sentences.en: I'm not, you know, a God on a throne.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我并不是高高在上的神。

sentences.en: That's the psychology understander that this is a collaborative process.
sentences.zh: 这就是心理学理解者所认为的，这是一个协作的过程。

sentences.en: And then I'm not concealing anything from them.
sentences.zh: 并且我没有对他们隐瞒任何事情。

sentences.en: And then I'm engaging them in their own treatment.
sentences.zh: 我还让他们参与到他们自己的治疗中。

sentences.en: You know, if you hand someone a bottle and you tell them plainly, it's a sugar pill and many of them still get better.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你递给某人一瓶药，并向他们坦白这只是糖丸，他们当中依然有许多人会好转。

sentences.en: So a placebo response doesn't have to be somebody being fooled because you can tell them that and it will still work.
sentences.zh: 因此，安慰剂效应并不意味着必须把人蒙在鼓里，因为即使你告诉了他们实情，它依然会起作用。

sentences.en: And second, when people respond to a placebo, their brains release their own natural painkillers and their feel good chemicals.
sentences.zh: 其次，当人们对安慰剂产生反应时，他们的大脑会释放自身天然的止痛药和快乐化学物质。

sentences.en: The same ones that drugs are designed to release mechanically, but who cares how they got released?
sentences.zh: 这与药物通过机械方式设计要释放的化学物质是同一种，但谁在乎它们是如何释放的呢？

sentences.en: The placebo and the drug are pulling the same lever and that breaks the basic math of what we think a trial is supposed to be.
sentences.zh: 安慰剂和药物拉动的是同一个杠杆，这就打破了我们对试验应有形态的基础数学认知。

sentences.en: I would argue because it breaks the math of what a patent for an antidepressant is supposed to be.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，因为它打破了抗抑郁药专利应有逻辑的基础数学。

sentences.en: So who is it that can pop the corn in the field?
sentences.zh: 那么，究竟是谁在田野里爆开玉米的呢？

sentences.en: What is the mechanism of action that is making the corn pop?
sentences.zh: 促使玉米爆开的作用机制究竟是什么？

sentences.en: The field measured who it was that could pop the corn too.
sentences.zh: 这个领域同时也测量了究竟是谁能够让玉米爆开。

sentences.en: In 1974, a researcher named David Ricks found that boys treated by one clinician did dramatically better in adult life than boys treated by others.
sentences.zh: 在1974年，一位名叫大卫·里克斯（David Ricks）的研究人员发现，由某位临床医生治疗的男孩在成年生活中的表现，比由其他医生治疗的男孩要好得多。

sentences.en: And he coined the word super shrink.
sentences.zh: 于是他创造了“超级心理治疗师”（super shrink）这个词。

sentences.en: In a modern study of 1,800 clients and 91 therapists, the best therapist clients improved about 10 times faster than average.
sentences.zh: 在对1800名客户和91名治疗师的现代研究中，最优秀治疗师的客户康复速度比平均水平快大约10倍。

sentences.en: And the worst therapist clients got worse.
sentences.zh: 而最糟糕治疗师的客户情况则变得更糟了。

sentences.en: A British study found recovery rates from 20 to 96%, depending only on which therapist you drew.
sentences.zh: 一项英国研究发现，康复率从20%到96%不等，这完全取决于你碰巧遇到了哪位治疗师。

sentences.en: The type of therapy, the degree that you held, the years of experience, explain none of it.
sentences.zh: 疗法的类型、你拥有的学位、从业年限，这些都无法解释这种差异。

sentences.en: Actually, in the largest data sets, therapists don't improve with experience.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在最大的数据集里，治疗师并不会随着经验的增加而变得更好。

sentences.en: They actually get slightly worse over time, especially the bad ones.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，他们的表现实际上会稍微变差一些，尤其是那些糟糕的治疗师。

sentences.en: The people who don't deal with their emotional blind spots, who won't heal their own damage,
sentences.zh: 那些不去处理自己情感盲点的人，那些不肯疗愈自身创伤的人——

sentences.en: because you can only take a patient as far as you can take yourself, tend to accumulate more of it
sentences.zh: 因为你只能把患者带到你自己所能达到的高度——往往会积累更多的问题，

sentences.en: and get more weird, more erratic, more rigid, and clinging tighter to paradigms that don't work when you watch them over time.
sentences.zh: 并且随着时间推移，当你观察他们时，他们会变得更加古怪、更加反复无常、更加死板，并且更紧紧地抓住那些不起作用的范式不放。

sentences.en: So it's not experience.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是经验的问题。

sentences.en: It's not training.
sentences.zh: 这不是培训的问题。

sentences.en: It's not education.
sentences.zh: 这不是学历的问题。

sentences.en: It's not what school you came from.
sentences.zh: 这无关乎你来自哪所学校。

sentences.en: It's not if you're an LPC, PsyD, clinical psychologist, social worker, LMFT, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 这无关乎你是不是LPC（持证专业咨询师）、PsyD（心理学博士）、临床心理学家、社工、LMFT（持证婚姻与家庭治疗师）等等。

sentences.en: So what is it?
sentences.zh: 那到底是什么呢？

sentences.en: What predicts it can be seen in the first week of therapy?
sentences.zh: 什么能够预测这一点，并且在治疗的第一周就能看出来？

sentences.en: Timothy Anderson's team showed graduate students videos of hard clinical moments.
sentences.zh: 蒂莫西·安德森（Timothy Anderson）的团队向研究生展示了艰难临床时刻的视频。

sentences.en: Maybe a patient attacked a provider over and over unprovoked verbally.
sentences.zh: 也许是一个患者无缘无故地在言语上一次又一次地攻击服务提供者。

sentences.en: Maybe a patient fell apart.
sentences.zh: 也许是一个患者彻底崩溃了。

sentences.en: They became unconsolable and wouldn't respond or listen when the therapist had another patient waiting outside and the hour was over and they were unable to stabilize them.
sentences.zh: 他们变得无法安慰，当治疗师外面还有另一个患者在等待、时间已经到了且无法让他们情绪稳定下来时，他们毫无反应也不听劝阻。

sentences.en: And they scored how warmly and steadily the therapist responded before their training had taught them anything at all.
sentences.zh: 研究人员对治疗师在他们的培训尚未教给他们任何东西之前，其反应是多么温暖和坚定进行评分。

sentences.en: This was a study conducting before the therapist went to school for the first class.
sentences.zh: 这是一项在治疗师去学校上第一堂课之前就进行的研究。

sentences.en: And more than a year later, those week one scores predicted how their patients did.
sentences.zh: 而在一年多以后，那些第一周的评分成功预测了他们患者的康复情况。

sentences.en: A German team found the same thing over five years to the ability is mostly there to be a super shrink before school starts.
sentences.zh: 一个德国团队在五年里也发现了同样的事情：在开学之前，成为一名超级治疗师的能力就已经基本具备了。

sentences.en: You know, it's put there by hands that nobody can really measure.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是由某些无法真正衡量的无形之手所赋予的。

sentences.en: And this is something that you will hear from many therapists.
sentences.zh: 而这也是你会从许多治疗师那里听到的说法。

sentences.en: There are some people that have something that can't be taught.
sentences.zh: 有些人确实具备某种无法被教导的东西。

sentences.en: And that thing that can't be taught is more important than anything that can.
sentences.zh: 而那种无法被教导的东西，比任何可以被教导的东西都要重要。

sentences.en: And they've always kind of known this, but graduate schools don't want to know that because they're supposed to teach you and make you better.
sentences.zh: 他们其实一直以来都有点心知肚明，但研究生院不想承认这一点，因为它们的职责本该是教导你并让你变得更优秀。

sentences.en: CEs don't want to know that because they're supposed to be continuing your education and keeping you relevant and up to date over time.
sentences.zh: 继续教育（CE）也不想知道这一点，因为它们本该持续推进你的教育，并随着时间推移让你保持专业相关性和与时俱进。

sentences.en: Um, patent companies don't want to hear this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，专利公司不想听到这个。

sentences.en: People who invent and study models or pay for models to be implemented like insurance companies don't
sentences.zh: 那些发明和研究模型的人，或者花钱让人去实施这些模型的人（比如保险公司），

sentences.en: want to hear that because surely the model is something that is scientific and increasingly good over time.
sentences.zh: 都不想听到这个，因为他们坚信模型必然是某种科学的、且随着时间推移不断完善的东西。

sentences.en: What we don't want to look at is the real evil in the profession.
sentences.zh: 我们最不愿意去审视的，其实是这个行业真正的弊病所在。

sentences.en: What is the bureaucracy that drives the good people out?
sentences.zh: 究竟是怎样的官僚体制把优秀的人才逼走的？

sentences.en: What are the incentive structures?
sentences.zh: 激励机制又是怎样的？

sentences.en: Namely, you know, the amount of paperwork, uh, the things that the super shrinks don't like, right?
sentences.zh: 也就是，你知道的，大量的文件工作，嗯，那些超级治疗师们所讨厌的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: That is what we should be getting rid of to make them stay.
sentences.zh: 这才是我们应该摆脱以留住他们的方式。

sentences.en: Last episode, I talked about those salt domes and that they sit next to the oil, uh, on all of the oil fields.
sentences.zh: 上集里，我谈到了那些盐丘，它们紧挨着所有油田里的石油，嗯。

sentences.en: And the, the Texas oil age started on top of one at spindle top in 1901.
sentences.zh: 得克萨斯州的石油时代就是于1901年在斯平德尔托普（Spindletop）的一个盐丘顶部拉开帷幕的。

sentences.en: I think 1901.
sentences.zh: 我想是1901年。

sentences.en: That's where the strategic petroleum reserve is stored in caverns inside of those salt domes, thousands of feet down.
sentences.zh: 战略石油储备就是储存在那些地下数千英尺深的盐丘内部洞穴里的。

sentences.en: You know, the thing that the U S uses to, you know, supposedly make sure that there's enough oil reserve that if the 1970s happens again,

sentences.en: and there's an oil shortage, we'll have it.

sentences.zh: 嗯，如果要在地面上建造数千个足球场大小的巨型炼油厂，成本实在太高了。

sentences.en: And because there's salt, which is pretty good at storing oil right next that goes down in these huge columns, right next to where, um, you
sentences.zh: 正因为有盐的存在——它非常适合储存石油——它们就在你，嗯，

sentences.en: mine oil because it's the salt that those domes welling up that push the little pockets of oil together.
sentences.zh: 开采石油的地方旁边形成巨大的柱状结构，因为正是那些向上涌动的盐丘把零散的油田挤压到了一起。

sentences.en: Um, you hollow them out and you store the oil or the, uh, yeah, the raw petroleum inside of this giant dome of salt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你把它们挖空，然后把石油或者说，嗯，原油储存在这个巨大的盐丘里面。

sentences.en: Storing it in steel tanks takes just hundreds and hundreds of open things of space.
sentences.zh: 把它们储存在钢制储罐里需要数百个开阔的空间。

sentences.en: They can get burned, bombed, electrical sparked.
sentences.zh: 它们可能会被烧毁、轰炸、产生电火花。

sentences.en: It's a lot less of a risk to put them underground.
sentences.zh: 把它们放在地下风险要小得多。

sentences.en: Um, and the salt seals the oil in and under pressure over time, um, salt will even close up its own small cracks with like more salt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，盐能够把石油密封在里面，而且随着时间的推移，在压力作用下，盐甚至会用更多的盐来封闭自身的微小裂缝。

sentences.en: So it's a perfect storage device.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个完美的储存装置。

sentences.zh: 然后当你想要把它重新填满时，你把水抽出来，再把更多的石油倒在上面，但是，那个，其实并没有什么大不了的问题。

sentences.zh: 如果你战略性地使用战略石油储备，当然我们现在并非如此，我们每天都在抽取它来压低价格，

sentences.en: And then we're grabbing more through deals and pumping it back in, which we've never really used it like before.
sentences.zh: 然后我们又通过交易获取更多石油并泵回地下，这在过去是从来没有过的用法。

sentences.en: You're not supposed to for a lot of reasons, but the reason you're not supposed to is that, uh, fresh water dissolves salt.
sentences.zh: 出于很多原因，你不应该这么做，但其中最主要的原因是，呃，淡水会溶解盐。

sentences.en: So like normally when you draw down, um, what's inside of, you know, the oil reserve by filling it with water, some of the salt will dissolve because it sees the fresh water and it
sentences.zh: 所以通常当你抽干石油储备时，也就是用注水的方式来替代原本由油占据的空间，一部分盐就会溶解，因为它遇到了淡水并

sentences.en: wants to equalize the pressure.
sentences.zh: 且想要平衡压力。

sentences.en: So it will dissolve as much salt into the water as the water can at that pressure.
sentences.zh: 因此，它会在该压力下将尽可能多的盐溶解到水中。

sentences.en: And then when it's dissolved as much as it can hold, it just sits there.
sentences.zh: 当溶解达到饱和无法再容纳更多时，它就停在那里。

sentences.en: It doesn't dissolve anymore.
sentences.zh: 它不再溶解了。

sentences.en: It's not a problem.
sentences.zh: 这本来不是个问题。

sentences.en: And then eventually the, the wall of salt like heals itself.
sentences.zh: 然后最终，盐壁会自我修复。

sentences.en: This is really how these things work.
sentences.zh: 事情确实是这样运作的。

sentences.en: I'm not reducing it that much.
